# Monsieur Dossier — French rental file, ready and protected, on Mac

> Monsieur Dossier is a Mac app that prepares and protects your French rental file (dossier de location): allowed documents, unneeded data hidden, each copy in the recipient’s name. In English and French, offline.

Language: English · [Version française](https://monsieurdossier.com/index.html.md) · [Web page](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/) · Updated: 23 November 2026

Drop in your documents. Monsieur Dossier sorts them, finds what to hide and prepares every copy in the recipient’s name, in one go. On your Mac, no account, nothing uploaded.

- No account
- 100% offline
- English and French
- Free beta
- Version 1.3.0, 26 November 2026
- [Download for Mac](https://github.com/doudandyx/monsieur-dossier-site/releases/latest/download/MonsieurDossier.dmg)

## Four steps, and the whole file is ready.

Allow about a minute per document.

1. **Drop everything in.** PDFs, scans, iPhone photos, or a whole folder. Each document is filed under its category. One a landlord isn’t allowed to ask for gets flagged. Paste the agency’s list: you see what’s missing.
2. **The masks are already placed.** IBAN, bank codes, social security numbers and passport MRZ lines are found in their common formats, on scans and photos too. You review and add your own. Masked text is destroyed on saving, not just covered.
3. **One watermark for every document.** Enter the agency and the property address: the wording is written for you and stays off verification QR codes. Change the recipient: every copy is redone.
4. **Everything saves in one go.** Every file is reopened and checked. If a check fails, it isn’t saved. One folder per send, and several documents can be combined into one file.

[See all the features](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/features.html)

## A rental file is a ready-made identity-theft kit.

ID, tax notice, payslips, address: it’s all there. Fake listings exist to collect it.

- **Fake listings.** A “landlord” asks for the full file before any viewing, then vanishes. Your documents are used to open credit lines or accounts.
- **Unprotected attachments.** A PDF sent by email gets forwarded, copied, and sits in inboxes for years.
- **Fake redaction.** A black box drawn in a PDF editor often leaves the text underneath, ready to copy. Blur can be reversed.

## The rental file, in plain terms.

In France, landlords pick tenants from a file of documents, the “dossier de location”. Here is what to know before you send it.

- **Four kinds of documents.** Identity, current address, occupation (contract, student status) and income (payslips, tax notice). The list is set by law.
- **Passport or residence permit.** Both count as ID. Monsieur Dossier finds the line of codes at the bottom of a passport (MRZ) so you can hide it. Your photo and name stay visible.
- **The guarantor.** Many landlords ask for one. Visale, a free guarantee from Action Logement, can stand in for it under conditions: check whether you qualify on [visale.fr](https://www.visale.fr/).
- **All in English.** The app and the watermark are available in English. Your documents are not translated: a landlord may ask for a translation.

## Nothing leaves your Mac. You can check.

Monsieur Dossier has no account, no server and no analytics. Turn off Wi-Fi: everything works the same.

- **100% local processing.** The app only talks to itself, on 127.0.0.1. No connection to the internet.
- **Hidden text is destroyed.** Each page is flattened into an image: what’s under a mask no longer exists in the file.
- **Metadata removed.** Author, software, creation dates: nothing from the original is copied over.
- **Your originals untouched.** New files are created. Yours are never changed.

**How it works without the internet.** Monsieur Dossier is a Python program installed on your Mac, with everything it needs inside. Your documents are recognised and the numbers to hide are found by fixed rules. Scans and photos are read by the text recognition built into macOS, also on your Mac. No online AI, no model to download.

## A landlord can’t ask for everything.

In France, [décret n° 2015-1437](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493) sets a limited list of documents for a main residence. Anything else is forbidden, and you can refuse it. When Monsieur Dossier recognises a document that isn’t on the list, it warns you.

**Allowed. Examples of documents they can ask for**

- One ID document (ID card, passport, residence permit)
- Proof of address (last 3 rent receipts, host certificate…)
- Employment contract or employer certificate
- Last 3 payslips
- Latest tax notice

**Forbidden. Examples of documents to refuse**

- Bank statements
- Carte Vitale (health card)
- Criminal record
- Medical records
- Signed direct-debit authorisation
- Any payment before the lease is signed

Indicative, non-exhaustive list. Reference: French décret n° 2015-1437 of 5 November 2015 (amended in 2019 and 2022), annexes I and II. Check the current text on [legifrance.gouv.fr](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493).

## Monsieur Dossier for Mac

Free beta. Free during the beta. For Intel and Apple Silicon Macs. Your documents stay on your Mac. Version 1.3.0, 26 November 2026.

[Download for Mac](https://github.com/doudandyx/monsieur-dossier-site/releases/latest/download/MonsieurDossier.dmg)

### On first launch

This beta is not yet validated by Apple. On first launch, macOS shows a warning: it means Apple has not checked the app, not that a problem was found. Four steps, once only.

1. **Install.** Open the downloaded file and drag Monsieur Dossier into the Applications folder.
2. **Open the app.** macOS shows the warning. Close it with “Done”: do not move the app to the Trash.
3. **Allow it.** In System Settings, open “Privacy & Security”, scroll down to “Security” and click “Open Anyway”. The button stays there for about an hour.
4. **Confirm.** Confirm with “Open Anyway”, then enter your Mac’s password. After that, the app opens normally.

Steps for macOS 15 and later. On an older version: right-click the app, then “Open”. A version validated by Apple is being prepared. It will open without these steps.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is Monsieur Dossier?

Monsieur Dossier is a Mac app that prepares the documents of a French rental file, the “dossier de location”. It sorts your documents, finds the numbers a landlord does not need in their common formats (IBAN, social security number, the passport’s line of codes) and places the masks, which you review. It then adds a watermark naming the recipient. Everything happens on your Mac, with no account and no internet connection.

### How is this different from DossierFacile?

DossierFacile is the government service: it verifies your file and shares it by link, without hiding anything. Monsieur Dossier verifies nothing: it protects the files you send yourself, by hiding what isn’t needed and naming the recipient. They work together. [See the detailed comparison](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/dossierfacile.html)

### Is Monsieur Dossier an official service?

No. It is an independent app, with no link to the French government or to DossierFacile. It does not certify your documents.

### Is the app available?

Yes, for Mac, as a free beta: download it from this page.

### Is there a version for Windows, iPhone or Android?

No. Monsieur Dossier runs only on Mac, with an Intel or Apple Silicon processor.

### Why does macOS show a warning on first launch?

Because this beta is not yet validated by Apple. The warning means Apple has not checked the app, not that a problem was found. One confirmation in System Settings is enough, once only.

### Are my documents sent anywhere?

No. Processing happens entirely on your Mac. The app has no server, creates no account and collects no analytics. It works without an internet connection.

### Can a landlord refuse a redacted copy?

No law settles it. Hide only what serves neither to assess your income nor to verify the document, and keep your originals: a landlord may ask to see them.

### Why not just blur?

Because blur and pixelation can be reversed. Only opaque masks are offered: a black bar, or a “frosted” look generated from random noise, never from what’s hidden.

### How do I know the file is safe?

After every export, the PDF is reopened and checked: no text, font, metadata or attachment left, and each masked area no longer resembles the original. If a check fails, the file isn’t saved.

### What should the watermark say?

The recipient, purpose and date, for example: “Copy – Rental application 12 rue des Lilas – For Agence Saône only – 11/2026”. A stolen copy becomes hard to reuse elsewhere.

### Should I hide the QR code on my tax notice?

No. The landlord uses it to check the document is genuine. QR codes and 2D-Doc are detected and kept free of watermark. You’re warned if a mask covers one, and the export checks they are still detected.

# Features: sort, redact, watermark — Monsieur Dossier

> What Monsieur Dossier does, step by step: sort your documents, find what is missing, hide, watermark, check and save.

Language: English · [Version française](https://monsieurdossier.com/fonctionnalites.html.md) · [Web page](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/features.html) · Updated: 23 November 2026

From a pile of files to a rental file ready to attach: what the app does at each step, and what it leaves for you to decide.

## 1. Drop everything in. It gets filed.

Drag your files or a whole folder into the window. Each document is read, recognised and sorted.

- **PDFs, scans and photos.** A PDF from your bank, a scan, an iPhone photo: they all work. A folder comes in with its subfolders.
- **Filed by category.** Identity, address, occupation, income: the four categories set by French law.
- **Several people.** Flatmates and guarantors each get their own file, in the same window.
- **Forbidden documents are flagged.** A bank statement or a health card? The app tells you a landlord isn’t allowed to ask for it, with the legal reference.

Good to know: the filing is a suggestion. You can move a document to another category.

## 2. Know what’s missing before you send.

Paste the list of documents the agency asked for. Monsieur Dossier compares it with what you already have.

- **Line by line.** Each requested document is marked provided or missing.
- **Text or image.** Paste the text of the email, or drop in a screenshot of the list.
- **Requests outside the legal list stand out.** If the agency asks for a document it isn’t allowed to require, you see it.

Good to know: the list is read on your Mac, like everything else.

## 3. The masks are already placed.

When you open a document, the numbers that have no place in a rental file are already covered. You review, add your own, and confirm.

- **Found for you.** IBAN, bank codes, social security number, card number, the passport’s line of codes: found in their common formats, on a PDF as well as a scan or a photo.
- **Each area is named.** “IBAN”, “Social security no.”: you know what is hidden, and why.
- **Your own areas.** Draw a box over anything you want to hide.
- **Hide everywhere.** After you draw an area, the same value is searched in all your documents and offered for hiding in one click.
- **Your signature, hidden by default.** A handwritten signature the app spots is hidden. One click shows it again if the landlord wants to see it.
- **Verification codes stay readable.** QR codes and 2D-Doc are left uncovered. You’re warned if a mask touches one.

Good to know: detection covers common formats, not every case. Review each document before you confirm it.

## 4. Send only the pages that matter.

A tax notice or a contract often has pages the landlord doesn’t need. Leave them out of the file you send.

- **One click removes a page.** One click puts it back.
- **Pages suggested for you.** Blank pages and general-information pages (terms, legal notices, “how to pay”) are suggested.
- **Never the pages that count.** The first page and pages carrying a verification code are not suggested.

Good to know: your original file is never changed.

## 5. A watermark naming the recipient, on every document.

Enter the agency and the property address. The wording is written for you and applied to the whole file.

- **The right wording, without writing it.** Recipient, purpose and date, for example: “Copy – Rental application 12 rue des Lilas – For Agence Saône only – 11/2026”.
- **A preview before you save.** You see the watermark on a page as you type.
- **Another recipient? Everything is redone.** Change the name: every copy is prepared again, and your masks stay in place.
- **Off the verification codes.** The watermark stays clear of QR codes and 2D-Doc, so the landlord can still check the document.
- **In French or English.** The wording follows the language you choose.

Good to know: your masks are kept as long as the app stays open.

## 6. Every file is checked before it is saved.

A mask that leaves the text underneath protects nothing. Monsieur Dossier checks that for you, file by file.

- **The hidden text no longer exists.** Each page is flattened into an image: what is under a mask is no longer in the file.
- **The file is reopened and checked.** No text, font, metadata or attachment left, and each hidden area no longer resembles the original. If a check fails, the file isn’t saved.
- **A second reading.** Each page is read again once masked. A sensitive number that is still readable is flagged, with a link to fix it.
- **Nothing from the original comes along.** Author, software, creation dates: no metadata is copied over.

Good to know: the second reading warns you, it does not block saving. The decision stays yours.

## 7. Everything saves in one go, ready to attach.

One click, one folder: the copies are named and combined the way you’re asked for them.

- **One folder per send.** Named after the agency, the address and the date.
- **Clear file names.** Each file is named after the document.
- **Combine the way the portal asks.** Your last three payslips as one file, the rest separate: drag the documents together.
- **A ZIP, if you prefer.** For a single attachment.
- **With several people.** One subfolder per person, flatmates and guarantors included.

Good to know: a send is prepared for one recipient at a time.

## 8. It all happens on your Mac.

None of these steps sends your documents anywhere.

- **No account, no server.** Nothing to create, nothing to connect.
- **A program, not a service.** Python code installed on your Mac. Numbers are found by fixed rules. Scans are read by the text recognition built into macOS, on your Mac. No online AI.
- **No connection needed.** Turn off Wi-Fi: everything works the same, reading scans included.
- **No usage tracking.** The app collects nothing.

## Prepare your rental file.

For Mac. No account, nothing uploaded. [Download for Mac](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/#download)

# Monsieur Dossier and DossierFacile: who does what

> Monsieur Dossier works alongside DossierFacile, the French government’s service: what each one does, and how to use them together.

Language: English · [Version française](https://monsieurdossier.com/dossierfacile.html.md) · [Web page](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/dossierfacile.html) · Updated: 23 November 2026

## It works alongside DossierFacile, not against it.

[DossierFacile](https://www.dossierfacile.logement.gouv.fr/), the French government’s free service, verifies your file and shares it by link. Monsieur Dossier protects the files you send yourself, when the link isn’t accepted or you’re asked for attachments.

| | DossierFacile | Monsieur Dossier |
|---|---|---|
| Its job | Verify your file and share it | Prepare and protect your files |
| Your documents | Uploaded to government servers, with an account | Stay on your Mac, no account |
| Verification | Yes: a government “verified” label | No: nothing is certified |
| Sharing | One revocable link per recipient | Files you attach yourself |
| Hidden data | None: complete documents required | IBAN, bank codes, social security no., MRZ, plus your own areas |
| Watermark | Fixed wording, no name or date | Recipient, address and date |
| Language | French | English and French |

## How to use them together

1. **Get verified.** Create your DossierFacile and share its link whenever the landlord accepts it.
2. **Protect the rest.** Asked for files by email or on a portal? Prepare them with Monsieur Dossier.
3. **Keep what’s checkable.** Never hide your tax number, the tax notice reference, QR codes or your photo.

Monsieur Dossier is an independent app. It is not a government service, is not affiliated with DossierFacile, and does not check that your documents are genuine.

# French rental file guides — Monsieur Dossier

> Short, sourced answers to the questions a French rental file raises: allowed documents, guarantors, watermarks, redaction, scams.

Language: English · [Version française](https://monsieurdossier.com/guides/index.html.md) · [Web page](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/) · Updated: 24 November 2026

## The French rental file, one question at a time.

Each guide answers one question, cites the law or the official source, and shows the date it was last updated.

- [What documents can a landlord ask for when you rent in France?](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/documents-landlord-can-ask-france.html) To rent a home in France, a landlord can ask for four kinds of documents: identity, current address, occupation and income. The list is set by decree.
- [What documents is a French landlord not allowed to ask for?](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/documents-landlord-cannot-ask-france.html) A French landlord cannot require any document outside the list set by decree: no bank statements, no health card, no criminal record, and no money to reserve the home.
- [Do I have to give my bank details (RIB) to rent in France?](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/bank-details-rib-rental-france.html) No. Your bank details (RIB) are not on the list of documents a French landlord can require before the lease is signed, and the CNIL names bank statements as off limits.
- [Can I rent a home in France without a guarantor?](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/rent-in-france-without-guarantor.html) Yes. French law does not require a guarantor, and Visale, a free guarantee from Action Logement, can stand in for one if you are aged up to 30 or a recent hire.
- [How do I put together a French rental file when I arrive from abroad?](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/rental-file-france-arriving-from-abroad.html) The same four kinds of documents, with what you have: passport or residence permit, employment contract, a foreign tax notice, all translated into French.
- [What should the watermark on my French rental documents say?](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/watermark-text-rental-documents-france.html) Write who the copy is for, what it is for and the date: that is the advice of Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr, the French government’s service, to keep a copy from being reused.
- [What can I hide on my French rental documents?](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/what-to-hide-rental-documents-france.html) No law settles it. Our reading: hide what serves neither to assess your file nor to verify the document, such as your IBAN or social security number. Never your tax number.
- [How do I redact a PDF on a Mac without uploading it?](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/redact-pdf-mac-without-uploading.html) With Preview, the app that comes with macOS: according to Apple, the Redaction Selection tool removes text from view, and the redaction becomes permanent once you close the document.
- [I sent my rental documents to a scammer in France: what do I do?](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/rental-documents-sent-to-scammer-france.html) Keep the evidence, tell your bank, report the listing and file a complaint. If an identity document went out, also file a “main courante” and watch your accounts.

---

# What documents can a landlord ask for when you rent in France?

> To rent a home in France, a landlord or agency can ask for four kinds of supporting documents: one identity document, one proof of your current address, one or more documents about your occupation, and one or more documents about your income. The list is set by [décret n° 2015-1437](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493) of 5 November 2015. A landlord cannot require a document that is not on it: according to [service-public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F1169), the French government’s information site, a landlord who does so risks a fine.

Language: English · [Version française](https://monsieurdossier.com/guides/documents-proprietaire-peut-demander.html.md) · [Web page](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/documents-landlord-can-ask-france.html) · Updated: 24 November 2026

## Which rentals does this list apply to?

It applies to homes rented as a main residence, furnished or unfurnished, and to the short “bail mobilité” lease: the [law of 6 July 1989](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000000509310/) extends the rule to all three. The [decree](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493) states that it does not apply to applications for social housing.

## Which identity document can a landlord ask for?

One valid identity document that carries your photo. [Annex I of the decree](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493) gives the list:

- a national identity card, French or foreign
- a passport, French or foreign
- a driving licence, French or foreign
- a document proving your right to stay in France, such as a temporary residence permit, a resident card or the card of a citizen of the European Union or the European Economic Area

## Which proof of address can a landlord ask for?

One proof of your current address, from those listed in the [decree](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493):

- your last three rent receipts, or failing that a statement from your previous landlord, or the landlord’s agent, that your rent and charges are paid up
- a certificate of domiciliation from an approved organisation
- a signed statement from the person who hosts you
- your latest property tax notice, or failing that the title deed of your main home

> The tenant’s list does not include an electricity, gas or water bill. Those bills are on the guarantor’s list.

## Which documents about your occupation can a landlord ask for?

One or more documents, depending on your situation. The list is the [decree](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493)’s:

- **Employee or intern.** The employment or internship contract, or failing that a letter from the employer stating the job, the proposed pay, the start date and, if there is one, the length of the trial period.
- **Student.** A student card or a certificate of enrolment for the current year.
- **Trading company.** A K or K bis extract from the company register, less than three months old.
- **Craft business.** The registration record in the Registre national des entreprises, less than three months old.
- **Self-employed.** A copy of the INSEE identification certificate.
- **Independent professional (profession libérale).** A copy of the professional card.
- **Other professionals.** Any recent document that proves the activity.

## Which documents about your income can a landlord ask for?

One or more documents, from those listed in the [decree](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493):

- your latest or second-latest tax notice, or notice of non-taxation. If all or part of your income was taxed in another country, the tax notice of that country or an equivalent document from its tax authority
- your last three payslips
- proof of payment of an internship allowance
- for the self-employed, the last two balance sheets, or failing that a statement of income for the current year drawn up by an accountant
- proof of payment over the last three months of benefits, pensions and allowances, or proof that the entitlement has been opened, issued by the paying body
- a housing benefit simulation, drawn up by the paying body or by you
- the grant award notice, for a student on a grant
- the title deed of a property, or the latest property tax notice
- proof of rental income, life annuities or investment income

## Do you have to hand over originals?

No. [Article 1 of the decree](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493) says the documents can be copies of the originals. They are written in French or translated into French, and amounts are converted into euros. The originals must be available if the landlord asks to see them.

## Which documents can a landlord ask the guarantor for?

The [decree](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493) sets a second list, in annex II, for the person who acts as guarantor: one identity document, one proof of address, and documents about occupation and income. For the address, the guarantor’s list is different: latest rent receipt, a water, gas or electricity bill less than three months old, a home insurance certificate less than three months old, the latest property tax notice or a title deed.

If the guarantor is a company or an organisation, the decree provides for a K bis extract less than three months old, the articles of association or another document proving that it legally exists, and proof of identity for its representative.

## What does a landlord risk by asking for anything else?

According to [service-public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F1169), a landlord or agency that demands a document outside the list risks a fine of up to €3,000, or €15,000 for a legal entity such as a company. [Article 22-2 of the law](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000000509310/) states that the fine is imposed by the prefect and that its amount depends on how serious the facts are.

The same article also bars a landlord from requiring an ascendant or a descendant of the applicant, a parent or a child for example, to co-sign. See [the documents a French landlord is not allowed to ask for](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/documents-landlord-cannot-ask-france.html).

## Sources

Sources checked on 24 November 2026.

- [Décret n° 2015-1437 of 5 November 2015, article 1 and annexes I and II (Légifrance, in French)](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493)
- [Loi n° 89-462 of 6 July 1989, articles 22-2, 25-3 and 25-12 (Légifrance, in French)](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000000509310/)
- [Documents a future tenant gives a private landlord (service-public.gouv.fr, page verified on 10 April 2025, in French)](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F1169)

This guide gives general information, current on the date shown. It is not legal advice: if in doubt, the law in force prevails.

## With Monsieur Dossier

Monsieur Dossier files your documents under these four categories and flags the ones a landlord is not allowed to ask for. Paste the list the agency sent you: you see what is missing, and what goes beyond the legal list. A Mac app, free during the beta. Your documents stay on your Mac. # What documents is a French landlord not allowed to ask for?

> A landlord or agency in France is not allowed to require any document outside the list set by [décret n° 2015-1437](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493) of 5 November 2015. The [CNIL](https://www.cnil.fr/fr/location-dun-bien-immobilier-quels-justificatifs), the French data protection authority, names among the documents you cannot be asked for: bank statements, the Carte Vitale health card, a criminal record extract, the family record book, a marriage contract and a divorce judgment. No money can be asked to reserve the home either. According to [service-public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F1169), the landlord or agency risks a fine of up to €3,000, or €15,000 for a legal entity.

Language: English · [Version française](https://monsieurdossier.com/guides/documents-interdits-dossier-location.html.md) · [Web page](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/documents-landlord-cannot-ask-france.html) · Updated: 24 November 2026

## Why are these documents forbidden?

Because the list of documents a landlord can require is set by law. The [law of 6 July 1989](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000000509310/) refers to a [decree](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493), which names the documents allowed for the applicant and for the guarantor. [Service-public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F1169) draws the consequence: a landlord who demands a document outside the list risks a fine. The full list is in the guide on [the documents a landlord can ask for](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/documents-landlord-can-ask-france.html).

## Which examples does the CNIL give?

The [CNIL](https://www.cnil.fr/fr/location-dun-bien-immobilier-quels-justificatifs) writes that estate agencies and landlords alike cannot ask for certain documents, such as:

- a copy of the family record book (livret de famille)
- the Carte Vitale health insurance card
- bank statements
- a marriage contract
- a divorce judgment
- a criminal record extract

> These are examples: the CNIL writes “such as”. The general rule is the decree’s. What is not on the list cannot be required.

## Which other documents are not on the list?

Other documents are sometimes asked for. None of the four below is in the [decree](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493), so none can be required. This is our reading of the list: the official pages we read do not name them one by one.

- your bank details (RIB), or a direct-debit authorisation signed in advance
- a letter from your bank about how your account is run
- medical records
- an identity photo, on top of the one on your identity document

## Can you be asked for money before the lease is signed?

No, according to [service-public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F1169): the landlord or agency is forbidden to ask for money in return for reserving the home, and no sum can be asked for before the lease is signed. The security deposit is paid at signing, says its [page on the security deposit](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F31269). The [law](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000000509310/) caps it at one month of rent excluding charges for an unfurnished home and two months for a furnished one.

## What does the landlord risk?

[Article 22-2 of the law](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000000509310/) provides for an administrative fine, imposed by the prefect of the département: at most €3,000 for an individual and €15,000 for a legal entity. The amount depends on how serious the facts are, and the fine can no longer be imposed more than a year after they were recorded. The [decree](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493) adds that the prefect first informs the landlord, who has two months to respond.

## What should you do if you are asked for a forbidden document?

1. State the rule in writing: the list of documents is set by [décret n° 2015-1437](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493).
2. Offer the allowed document that meets the same need, for example your tax notice instead of a bank statement.
3. Keep a record of the request: email, message, screenshot of the listing.
4. If the request stands, ask the ADIL, the housing information agency of your département, which [service-public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F1169) gives as a contact. You can also write to the prefect of your département, since the prefect is the one who imposes the fine.

> These four steps are our advice. No official page we read describes how to report an illegal request.

## Sources

Sources checked on 24 November 2026.

- [Décret n° 2015-1437 of 5 November 2015, articles 1 and 1-1 (Légifrance, in French)](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493)
- [Loi n° 89-462 of 6 July 1989, articles 22, 22-2 and 25-6 (Légifrance, in French)](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000000509310/)
- [Documents a future tenant gives a private landlord (service-public.gouv.fr, page verified on 10 April 2025, in French)](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F1169)
- [Renting a property: which supporting documents? (CNIL, 10 October 2025, in French)](https://www.cnil.fr/fr/location-dun-bien-immobilier-quels-justificatifs)
- [Security deposit in a residential lease (service-public.gouv.fr, page verified on 9 June 2026, in French)](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F31269)

# Do I have to give my bank details (RIB) to rent in France?

> No, you do not have to give your bank details to apply for a rental in France. The RIB, the slip that shows your IBAN, is not on the list of documents a landlord can require from an applicant, set by [décret n° 2015-1437](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493). We infer this from the list: no official page we read names the RIB. The [CNIL](https://www.cnil.fr/fr/location-dun-bien-immobilier-quels-justificatifs), for its part, names bank statements among the documents that cannot be asked for. Once the lease is signed, you give your RIB if you choose direct debit, which the [law](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000000509310/) forbids forcing on you.

Language: English · [Version française](https://monsieurdossier.com/guides/rib-dossier-location.html.md) · [Web page](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/bank-details-rib-rental-france.html) · Updated: 24 November 2026

## What does a landlord use a RIB for?

To set up a direct debit for the rent. That need only exists once the lease is signed. Before that, a RIB says nothing about your income: for that, the [decree](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493) lists proof of income, such as your payslips or your tax notice.

## Can a landlord impose direct debit?

No. Article 4 of the [law of 6 July 1989](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000000509310/) treats as void any clause that imposes automatic direct debit from the tenant’s account as the way to pay the rent. [Service-public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F1686) lists it among the clauses forbidden in a lease. You can choose direct debit, but it cannot be forced on you.

## Can a landlord ask for bank statements?

No. The [CNIL](https://www.cnil.fr/fr/location-dun-bien-immobilier-quels-justificatifs), the French data protection authority, names bank statements among the documents that agencies and landlords alike cannot ask for, along with the Carte Vitale health card and a criminal record extract. A letter from your bank about how your account is run is not on the [decree](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493)’s list either.

## My IBAN shows on another document: what should I do?

A payslip sometimes shows the IBAN of the account your salary is paid into. In our view, the landlord does not need it to assess your file. You can hide it before you send the copy: see [what you can hide on your documents](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/what-to-hide-rental-documents-france.html).

## What should you answer if you are asked for your RIB anyway?

- Point out that the RIB is not among the documents listed in [décret n° 2015-1437](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493).
- Offer to hand it over when the lease is signed, if you choose direct debit.
- If you are asked for your papers before any viewing, be careful: [service-public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F34092) lists a request for official documents before the viewing, an identity card for example, among the signs of a fake listing. See [what to do if your file went to a scammer](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/rental-documents-sent-to-scammer-france.html).

## Sources

Sources checked on 24 November 2026.

- [Décret n° 2015-1437 of 5 November 2015, annexes I and II (Légifrance, in French)](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493)
- [Loi n° 89-462 of 6 July 1989, article 4 (Légifrance, in French)](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000000509310/)
- [Forbidden clauses in a residential lease (service-public.gouv.fr, page verified on 1 October 2026, in French)](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F1686)
- [Renting a property: which supporting documents? (CNIL, 10 October 2025, in French)](https://www.cnil.fr/fr/location-dun-bien-immobilier-quels-justificatifs)
- [Rental scams on the internet (service-public.gouv.fr, page verified on 16 October 2024, in French)](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F34092)

This guide gives general information, current on the date shown. It is not legal advice: if in doubt, the law in force prevails.

You review each document. A Mac app, free during the beta. Your documents stay on your Mac. [Download for Mac](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/#download)

# Can I rent a home in France without a guarantor?

> Yes, you can rent in France without a guarantor. The law does not require a tenant to have one: it is the landlord who chooses to ask. If nobody close to you can act as guarantor, [Visale](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F33453), a guarantee from Action Logement, can stand in for one. It is free and open to people aged up to 30, to some older employees and to tenants on a “bail mobilité” lease. You have to apply before you sign the lease.

Language: English · [Version française](https://monsieurdossier.com/guides/louer-sans-garant.html.md) · [Web page](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/rent-in-france-without-guarantor.html) · Updated: 24 November 2026

## Can a landlord insist on a guarantor?

Yes, the [law of 6 July 1989](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000000509310/) allows it, within limits set in its articles 22-1 and 22-2.

- A landlord who has taken out insurance against unpaid rent cannot ask for a guarantor as well, unless the tenant is a student or an apprentice.
- A landlord cannot refuse a guarantor on the ground that the person is not French or does not live in mainland France.
- A landlord cannot require an ascendant or a descendant of the applicant, a parent or a child for example, to co-sign the lease.
- When the landlord is a company, other than a family property company, it can ask for a guarantor only if the guarantee comes from a body on a list set by decree, or if the home is let to a student who does not receive a higher-education grant.

> In practice, [DossierFacile](https://www.dossierfacile.logement.gouv.fr/blog/etudiant-etranger-logement), the government service, writes that some landlords accept a guarantor living abroad, but that this remains rare.

## What is the Visale guarantee?

Visale is a free guarantee granted by [Action Logement](https://www.actionlogement.fr/la-garantie-visale). If rent goes unpaid or the home is damaged, Action Logement first pays the landlord the sum owed, then gets it back from the tenant.

According to [service-public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F33453), it covers at most 36 months of unpaid rent during the first three years of the lease, and damage up to two months of rent and charges. You apply online, before signing the lease. You receive a “visa” to hand to the landlord. For the guarantee to apply, the landlord must then accept the guarantee deed.

## Who can get Visale?

According to [service-public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F33453) and [Action Logement](https://www.actionlogement.fr/la-garantie-visale), read on 24 November 2026:

- people aged 30 and under, whatever their work situation, students and work-study trainees included
- older private-sector employees, if their net pay does not exceed €1,710 a month, or if they have just been hired or transferred and apply within six months
- tenants who sign a “bail mobilité” lease, whatever their age

The rent, charges included, is capped: €1,940 in the Paris region, €1,575 or €1,365 elsewhere depending on the town. An income condition applies depending on your situation, and lower caps apply to students and work-study trainees who cannot show proof of income. The official eligibility test, on [service-public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F33453), gives the answer for your case.

## Is Visale open to international students?

Yes, according to [Campus France](https://www.campusfrance.org/en/VISALE-free-rental-deposit-for-students): you only need to be between 18 and 30. A student who needs a visa to come to France must have obtained a long-stay visa that serves as a residence permit, marked “étudiant” or “passeport talent”. A student who is a citizen of a European Union country shows a student card and a valid passport. Campus France recommends starting the application as soon as the visa is issued.

## What are the other options without a guarantor?

- **A bank guarantee.** According to [DossierFacile](https://www.dossierfacile.logement.gouv.fr/blog/etudiant-etranger-logement), you can deposit a sum with a French bank, which serves as security if rent goes unpaid.
- **A legal entity.** According to [service-public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F31267), the guarantor can be a person, such as a parent or a friend, or a legal entity: Action Logement, a company, a bank.
- **The “bail mobilité” lease.** Under the [law](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000000509310/), a lease of one to ten months for a furnished home, reserved for people in higher education, on an internship, in an apprenticeship, in vocational training, in civic service, on a job transfer or on a temporary assignment. The landlord cannot ask for a security deposit.

## What money can a landlord ask for?

No sum before the lease is signed, according to [service-public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F1169). After that, the [law](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000000509310/) caps the security deposit at one month of rent excluding charges for an unfurnished home and two months for a furnished one, and forbids it for a “bail mobilité”. If rent is payable more than two months in advance, no security deposit is allowed.

## Which documents can a guarantor be asked for?

According to [décret n° 2015-1437](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493): one identity document, one proof of address, and documents about occupation and income. The list is in the guide on [the documents a landlord can ask for](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/documents-landlord-can-ask-france.html).

## Sources

Sources checked on 24 November 2026.

- [Visale guarantee (service-public.gouv.fr, page verified on 23 January 2026, in French)](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F33453)
- [The Visale guarantee (Action Logement, in French)](https://www.actionlogement.fr/la-garantie-visale)
- [A tenant’s guarantor in private housing (service-public.gouv.fr, page verified on 10 April 2025, in French)](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F31267)
- [Loi n° 89-462 of 6 July 1989, articles 22, 22-1, 22-2, 25-6, 25-12 to 25-17 (Légifrance, in French)](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000000509310/)
- [Future tenant: documents to give the landlord (service-public.gouv.fr, page verified on 10 April 2025, in French)](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F1169)

# How do I put together a French rental file when I arrive from abroad?

> When you arrive from abroad, your French rental file, the “dossier de location”, holds the same four kinds of documents as any other applicant’s, using the papers you have. A passport or a residence permit serves as your identity document. An employment contract, or a letter from your employer, proves your occupation. If your income was taxed in another country, [décret n° 2015-1437](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493) provides for that country’s tax notice. The documents must be written in French or translated into French, with amounts converted into euros.

Language: English · [Version française](https://monsieurdossier.com/guides/dossier-location-arrivee-etranger.html.md) · [Web page](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/rental-file-france-arriving-from-abroad.html) · Updated: 24 November 2026

## Which identity document should you provide?

One valid document showing your photo: a passport, an identity card or a driving licence, French or foreign, or a document proving your right to stay in France, such as a residence permit or a resident card. This is the [decree](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493)’s list.

## What can you provide without a French tax notice?

The [decree](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493) covers this: when all or part of your income was taxed in another country, the document is that country’s tax notice, or an equivalent document from its tax authority. You can also prove your income with other documents on the list, for example a grant award notice.

## What can you provide without French payslips?

The [decree](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493) lists the “last three payslips” without naming a country. Our reading: foreign payslips, translated, can be presented. If you are starting a job, the employment or internship contract is on the list of documents about your occupation. Failing that, a letter from the employer states the job, the proposed pay, the start date and, if there is one, the length of the trial period. A student provides a student card or a certificate of enrolment for the current year.

## Do you have to translate your documents?

Yes. The [decree](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493) requires documents written in French or translated into French, with amounts converted into euros. It does not say who must translate. [DossierFacile](https://www.dossierfacile.logement.gouv.fr/blog/etudiant-etranger-logement), the government service, writes in its blog that it accepts sworn translations, and that you can also translate the key points yourself, directly on the document. That flexibility is DossierFacile’s: a landlord may ask for more.

## What if you have no guarantor in France?

[Visale](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F33453), the free guarantee from Action Logement, can stand in for a guarantor. You apply before signing the lease. According to [Campus France](https://www.campusfrance.org/en/VISALE-free-rental-deposit-for-students), a student aged 18 to 30 who needs a visa to come to France must have obtained a long-stay visa that serves as a residence permit, marked “étudiant” or “passeport talent”, and can start the application as soon as that visa is issued. The other options are in the guide on [renting without a guarantor](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/rent-in-france-without-guarantor.html).

## Where should you start?

1. Gather one identity document, one document about your occupation and one about your income.
2. Translate into French anything that is not, and convert the amounts into euros.
3. Apply for the Visale visa if you qualify: you show it to the landlord with your file.
4. Create a file on DossierFacile if the landlord accepts its link. In [its blog](https://www.dossierfacile.logement.gouv.fr/blog/etudiant-etranger-logement), the service names the passport or the residence permit as the identity document.
5. Pay nothing before the lease is signed: according to [service-public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F1169), a landlord has no right to ask.
6. Protect the copies you send by email: see [what the watermark should say](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/watermark-text-rental-documents-france.html).

> For a stay of one to ten months during higher education, an internship, an apprenticeship, vocational training, civic service, a job transfer or a temporary assignment, the [“bail mobilité” lease](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F34759) is an option: the home is furnished and, under the [law](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000000509310/), the landlord cannot ask for a security deposit.

- [Documents a future tenant gives a private landlord (service-public.gouv.fr, page verified on 10 April 2025, in French)](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F1169)
- [International students looking for housing (DossierFacile blog, 12 May 2025, in French)](https://www.dossierfacile.logement.gouv.fr/blog/etudiant-etranger-logement)

- [Visale guarantee (service-public.gouv.fr, page verified on 23 January 2026, in French)](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F33453)

# What should the watermark on my French rental documents say?

> Write three things in the watermark on your French rental documents: who the copy is for, what it is for, and the date. This is the advice of [Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr](https://www.cybermalveillance.gouv.fr/tous-nos-contenus/fiches-reflexes/arnaques-location-immobiliere), the French government’s cybersecurity help service, which recommends writing on each copy the reason for sending it, the date and the recipient, so that it cannot be reused for fraud. An example, written by us: “Copy – Rental application 12 rue des Lilas – For Agence Saône only – 11/2026”.

Language: English · [Version française](https://monsieurdossier.com/guides/texte-filigrane-dossier-location.html.md) · [Web page](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/watermark-text-rental-documents-france.html) · Updated: 24 November 2026

## Why name the recipient and date the copy?

[Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr](https://www.cybermalveillance.gouv.fr/tous-nos-contenus/fiches-reflexes/arnaques-location-immobiliere) recommends it to keep your documents from being reused for fraud. Our explanation: a general phrase does not say where the copy came from. [FiligraneFacile](https://filigrane.beta.gouv.fr/), the government’s watermarking service, suggests “Document exclusivement destiné à la location immobilière”, meaning for property rental only. Such a phrase limits the use, but it would still hold for another rental. With the name of the agency or landlord and the date, each copy is tied to a single send.

## Which wording should you use?

No official page gives a wording with recipient and date. The three examples below are ours: one short, readable line with the recipient, the purpose and the month.

- for an agency: “Copy – Rental application 12 rue des Lilas – For Agence Saône only – 11/2026”
- for a private landlord: “Copy – Rental 5 place Carnot – For Mr Durand only – 11/2026”
- in French: “Copie – Dossier location 12 rue des Lilas – Usage exclusif Agence Saône – 11/2026”

> [FiligraneFacile](https://filigrane.beta.gouv.fr/) limits the text to 100 characters. All three examples fit within that limit.

## Where should the watermark go?

[Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr](https://www.cybermalveillance.gouv.fr/tous-nos-contenus/fiches-reflexes/usurpation-identite-que-faire) speaks of writing the mention “over” the copy. Our advice goes the same way: across the whole page, repeated, over the text, because a mention placed in a margin can be cropped out. The document must stay readable. Do not cover the 2D-Doc code on a tax notice: according to [impots.gouv.fr](https://www.impots.gouv.fr/precisions-sur-le-service-de-verification-en-ligne), it is used to check that the notice has not been altered.

## Which tool can add a watermark?

- **[FiligraneFacile](https://filigrane.beta.gouv.fr/)**, the government’s online service. You upload a jpg, png, heic or pdf file, type the text and get a PDF back. The service says it erases the originals from its servers once the file is generated, and the watermarked file after its first download, or after one day. The [CNIL](https://www.cnil.fr/fr/location-dun-bien-immobilier-quels-justificatifs), the French data protection authority, presents it as a way to protect sensitive documents before sending them.
- **DossierFacile**, the government’s service for rental files. [Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr](https://www.cybermalveillance.gouv.fr/tous-nos-contenus/fiches-reflexes/arnaques-location-immobiliere) names it, with FiligraneFacile, among the official sites that help secure a file or mark copies with a watermark.
- **[France Identité](https://france-identite.gouv.fr/justificatif/)**, the government’s app. It creates a single-use proof of identity: a PDF signed by the Interior Ministry, for which you set a recipient, a duration and a purpose, in place of a photocopy of your identity document. The conditions for using it are on its site.

## Is a watermark enough to protect a copy?

No, in our view. A watermark deters misuse and shows where a copy came from, but image retouching can fade or remove it. It does not replace hiding the numbers the landlord does not need: see [what you can hide on your documents](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/what-to-hide-rental-documents-france.html).

## Can a watermarked document be refused?

Yes, it can happen. [FiligraneFacile](https://filigrane.beta.gouv.fr/) says so itself: adding a watermark is good practice, but some organisations, such as banks or public services, may need a clean document. Always keep your originals.

## Sources

Sources checked on 24 November 2026.

- [How to react to a rental scam (Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr, page updated on 28 October 2026, in French)](https://www.cybermalveillance.gouv.fr/tous-nos-contenus/fiches-reflexes/arnaques-location-immobiliere)
- [Renting a property: which supporting documents? (CNIL, 10 October 2025, in French)](https://www.cnil.fr/fr/location-dun-bien-immobilier-quels-justificatifs)

# What can I hide on my French rental documents?

> No law sets out what an applicant can hide on French rental documents. Our reading: you can hide what serves neither to assess your file nor to verify the document, such as your IBAN, your social security number or the line of codes at the bottom of a passport. Leave visible your tax number, the tax notice reference and the 2D-Doc code, which are used to verify the notice, plus your photo, name and income. As far as we know, nothing obliges a landlord to accept a redacted copy, and [décret n° 2015-1437](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493) lets them ask for the original.

Language: English · [Version française](https://monsieurdossier.com/guides/masquer-informations-dossier-location.html.md) · [Web page](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/what-to-hide-rental-documents-france.html) · Updated: 24 November 2026

## What does a landlord not need to see?

This is our reading, not a written rule. These three items serve neither to assess your ability to pay nor to verify the document:

- **Your IBAN and bank details (RIB)**, which a payslip sometimes shows. The RIB is not on the [decree](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493)’s list.
- **Your social security number**, which a payslip may contain. About a different case, the [CNIL](https://www.cnil.fr/sites/default/files/2025-11/logement_social-fiche04.pdf) counts it among the payslip data that are in principle not needed.
- **The line of codes at the bottom of a passport or identity card**, called the MRZ, which repeats your details in a machine-readable form.

> For a social housing application the rules are different: according to the [CNIL](https://www.cnil.fr/sites/default/files/2025-11/logement_social-fiche04.pdf), the social security number of the adults who will live in the home is part of the information requested.

## What must stay visible?

- **Your tax number and the tax notice reference.** According to [impots.gouv.fr](https://www.impots.gouv.fr/precisions-sur-le-service-de-verification-en-ligne), these are the two thirteen-digit identifiers to type into the tax notice verification service, which a landlord can use.
- **The 2D-Doc code.** According to impots.gouv.fr, the code printed on the tax notice is used to check that the notice has not been altered. Likewise, leave any verification QR code.
- **Your photo and your name**, on the identity document: the [decree](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493) asks for a document that carries its holder’s photograph.
- **Your income, your employer and the dates**: this is what serves to assess the file.

## Are you allowed to hide part of a document?

As far as we know, no law settles it. [Décret n° 2015-1437](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493) allows copies, and says the originals must be available if the landlord asks for them. Our advice: hide little, say that you did, and keep your originals.

The [CNIL](https://www.cnil.fr/sites/default/files/2025-11/logement_social-fiche04.pdf), the French data protection authority, has commented on a neighbouring case, which is not that of a rental applicant. About the payslips of their own staff that social landlords pass on to justify service charges, it notes that the social security number or the address are in principle not needed, and that sharing them can breach the principle of data minimisation unless all the irrelevant items are redacted.

## Why is a black box not enough?

Because a box drawn in a PDF editor can leave the text underneath, where it can still be copied. Blur and pixelation can sometimes be reversed. These are general technical observations, which the pages cited here do not cover. When in doubt, check: a reliable mask removes the information from the file. See [how to redact a PDF on a Mac](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/redact-pdf-mac-without-uploading.html).

## How do you check that a mask holds?

1. Open the redacted copy.
2. Try to select the text under the mask, then to copy it.
3. Search for the hidden number with the search function.
4. If the text can be copied or found, the mask removed nothing: start again with another tool.

## What if the landlord refuses the redacted copy?

Show the original at the viewing or at signing: the [decree](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493) says originals can be asked for. You can also go through DossierFacile, the government service: according to the [CNIL](https://www.cnil.fr/fr/location-dun-bien-immobilier-quels-justificatifs), it lets the tenant upload the authorised documents and pass them on to the landlord.

- [Décret n° 2015-1437 of 5 November 2015, article 1 and annex I (Légifrance, in French)](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000031444493)
- [About the tax notice verification service (impots.gouv.fr, page modified on 6 January 2026, in French)](https://www.impots.gouv.fr/precisions-sur-le-service-de-verification-en-ligne)
- [Social housing guide, sheet 4: which data may be collected? (CNIL, PDF in French)](https://www.cnil.fr/sites/default/files/2025-11/logement_social-fiche04.pdf)

QR codes and 2D-Doc stay readable, and you are warned if a mask touches one. Detection does not cover every case: you review each document. A Mac app, free during the beta. # How do I redact a PDF on a Mac without uploading it?

> On a Mac, you can redact a PDF without uploading it by using Preview, the app that comes with macOS. Show the Markup toolbar, choose the Redaction Selection tool, then select the text to hide. According to [Apple](https://support.apple.com/guide/preview/annotate-a-pdf-prvw11580/mac), you can still change the redaction while the document is open, and it becomes permanent once the document is closed. Apple does not say whether the text is erased from the file: work on a copy, then check that the hidden text can no longer be selected or found.

Language: English · [Version française](https://monsieurdossier.com/guides/caviarder-pdf-mac.html.md) · [Web page](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/redact-pdf-mac-without-uploading.html) · Updated: 24 November 2026

## Why redact on your Mac instead of online?

Many online tools receive your file on their servers to process it. For a payslip or an identity document, that is one more copy out of your control. Preview is an app installed on your Mac: it opens and edits the file in place. This is a general observation, which the Apple page cited here does not cover.

## How do you redact a PDF with Preview, step by step?

1. Duplicate the file and open the copy in Preview: according to [Apple](https://support.apple.com/guide/preview/annotate-a-pdf-prvw11580/mac), the redaction becomes permanent on closing.
2. Show the Markup toolbar, if it is not already visible.
3. Choose the Redaction Selection tool. That is its name in the Preview guide for macOS 27.
4. Select the text to hide. Repeat for each number.
5. Close the document, then run the checks described below.

## What are the limits of Preview’s tool?

- [Apple](https://support.apple.com/guide/preview/annotate-a-pdf-prvw11580/mac) describes the tool this way: “Select text to remove it from view.” Its page does not say that the text is removed from the file, hence the checks below.
- It applies to text that can be selected. Apple does not describe using it on a scanned PDF, where the text is an image.
- According to Apple, if the PDF has a table of contents, the entries that link to redacted text are not removed.
- You find each number yourself, on every page of every document.

## Is drawing a black box the same thing?

No. A shape drawn over the text covers it without removing it: the text can stay in the file, where it can still be selected and copied. This is a general technical observation, which Apple’s page does not cover. Use the redaction tool, then check.

## How do you check that the text is really gone?

1. Reopen the redacted file.
2. Try to select the hidden area and copy its content.
3. Search for the hidden number with Command + F.
4. If the text can be copied or found, do not send the file. If nothing can be copied and the search finds nothing, the text can no longer be read by these means.

## What about a photo or a scan?

For an image, [Apple](https://support.apple.com/guide/preview/annotate-a-pdf-prvw11580/mac) describes the Rectangular Selection tool, which selects an area to copy or delete. For a scanned PDF, its page describes no method. In both cases, check the result before you send it: see [what you can hide on your documents](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/what-to-hide-rental-documents-france.html).

## Sources

Sources checked on 24 November 2026.

- [Annotate a PDF in Preview on Mac (Apple Support, Preview guide for macOS 27)](https://support.apple.com/guide/preview/annotate-a-pdf-prvw11580/mac)

This guide gives general information, current on the date shown. It is not legal advice: if in doubt, the law in force prevails.

## With Monsieur Dossier

Monsieur Dossier does this across the whole file. It finds the IBAN, bank codes, social security number and the passport’s line of codes in their common formats, on a scan or a photo too, then flattens each page into an image so that the hidden text no longer exists. Every file is reopened and checked before it is saved. It all happens on your Mac. A Mac app, free during the beta. Your documents stay on your Mac. [Download for Mac](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/#download)

# I sent my rental documents to a scammer in France: what do I do?

> If you sent your French rental file to a fake landlord, [Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr](https://www.cybermalveillance.gouv.fr/tous-nos-contenus/fiches-reflexes/arnaques-location-immobiliere), the French government’s help service for victims, recommends keeping all the evidence, telling your bank, reporting the listing to the platform that carries it, then filing a complaint. If you paid money, ask your bank to stop the payment as fast as you can. If you sent a copy of an identity document, also file a “main courante”, a dated police record. Your documents can be used to open an account or take out a loan in your name: the [Banque de France](https://www.banque-france.fr/fr/a-votre-service/particuliers/agir-usurpation-identite) explains how to check.

Language: English · [Version française](https://monsieurdossier.com/guides/dossier-location-envoye-escroc.html.md) · [Web page](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/rental-documents-sent-to-scammer-france.html) · Updated: 24 November 2026

## What should you do right away?

[Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr](https://www.cybermalveillance.gouv.fr/tous-nos-contenus/fiches-reflexes/arnaques-location-immobiliere), the French government’s help service for victims, gives these steps, in this order:

1. **Keep the evidence**: screenshots of the listing, messages, bank statements.
2. **Tell your bank** and check the transactions on your account regularly.
3. **If you paid money**, by transfer, cheque or card, ask your bank to stop the payment as fast as you can, to try to block the transaction.
4. **Report the listing** to the platform that published it.
5. **File a complaint**, with all your evidence.
6. **If you sent a copy of an identity document, file a “main courante”** at a police station or a gendarmerie. It puts the facts on record for later action.

## Where can you file a complaint or get advice?

- **THESEE**, the online service for reporting an internet scam, and for filing a complaint if you are an adult. According to [service-public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/R47990), two conditions must both be met: you never met the scammer in person, and they asked you for money, whether or not you paid. A report is not a complaint.
- **The [online complaint service](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/R19620)** of the Interior Ministry, for an offence against property, fraud included, when the offender is unknown. A police officer or gendarme may ask you to come in and complete your statement.
- **A police station or a gendarmerie**, or a letter to the public prosecutor.
- **France Victimes**, on 116 006. The call is free, and the association can support you through the steps ([Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr](https://www.cybermalveillance.gouv.fr/tous-nos-contenus/fiches-reflexes/arnaques-location-immobiliere)).
- **Info Escroqueries**, on 0 805 805 817. The call is free, Monday to Friday from 9 am to 6.30 pm ([Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr](https://www.cybermalveillance.gouv.fr/tous-nos-contenus/fiches-reflexes/arnaques-location-immobiliere)).
- **[17Cyber](https://17cyber.gouv.fr)**, the online help service of the police, the gendarmerie and Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr.

According to [service-public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F34092), fraud is punished by five years in prison and a €375,000 fine, and you have six years to file a complaint, counted from the last act of fraud.

## How do you protect yourself against identity theft?

The [Banque de France](https://www.banque-france.fr/fr/a-votre-service/particuliers/agir-usurpation-identite) and [Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr](https://www.cybermalveillance.gouv.fr/tous-nos-contenus/fiches-reflexes/usurpation-identite-que-faire) advise you to:

- tell all your banks, and your employer if you sent payslips
- ask for the list of accounts opened in your name in the Ficoba register, through the secure messaging in your impots.gouv.fr account or by post to your tax office
- check with the Banque de France that you are not listed in its register of cheque incidents (FCC) or its register of loan repayment incidents (FICP), and repeat the check from time to time. For more information, the Banque de France gives the number 34 14
- file a complaint for each use of your identity. According to Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr, identity theft carries up to one year in prison and a €15,000 fine
- have an identity document that scammers used cancelled and renewed

[Service-public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F37944) separates two cases. If you only suspect identity theft, you can file a “main courante”. As soon as your identity is used without your knowledge, you can file a complaint.

## Should you tell your guarantor?

Yes, in our view, if you also sent their documents. The official pages we read do not mention it. Their documents face the same risk as yours, and they can take the same steps in their own name.

## How do you recognise a fake listing?

[Service-public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F34092) lists these signs:

- a very low price for the location, size or standard of the home
- photos that appear in another listing
- a landlord who behaves oddly, for example by refusing to meet you
- a request for money before the lease is signed
- a request for official documents, an identity card for example, before the viewing

[Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr](https://www.cybermalveillance.gouv.fr/tous-nos-contenus/fiches-reflexes/arnaques-location-immobiliere) adds three pieces of advice. Refuse any payment to an account abroad, in cash or through a money transfer service. Wait until you receive the keys to pay the security deposit and the first rent, by bank transfer or by cheque. If in any doubt, ask the landlord for a copy of their property tax notice, to make sure the home is really theirs.

## How do you protect the next copies you send?

[Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr](https://www.cybermalveillance.gouv.fr/tous-nos-contenus/fiches-reflexes/arnaques-location-immobiliere) recommends marking each copy with the reason for sending it, the date and the recipient, and handing documents over in person when you can. You can also hide what the recipient does not need. See [what the watermark should say](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/watermark-text-rental-documents-france.html) and [what you can hide on your documents](https://monsieurdossier.com/en/guides/what-to-hide-rental-documents-france.html).

## Sources

Sources checked on 24 November 2026.

- [How to react to a rental scam (Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr, page updated on 28 October 2026, in French)](https://www.cybermalveillance.gouv.fr/tous-nos-contenus/fiches-reflexes/arnaques-location-immobiliere)
- [Identity theft: what to do (Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr, page updated on 23 September 2026, in French)](https://www.cybermalveillance.gouv.fr/tous-nos-contenus/fiches-reflexes/usurpation-identite-que-faire)
- [Rental scams on the internet (service-public.gouv.fr, page verified on 16 October 2024, in French)](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F34092)
- [Report a rental scam (fake listing), THESEE (service-public.gouv.fr, page verified on 28 November 2024, in French)](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/R47990)
- [Online complaint (service-public.gouv.fr, page verified on 23 October 2024, in French)](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/R19620)
